newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks end softer after five days of gain.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks end softer after five days of gain.

text.p: Taiwan share prices closed slightly lower on Monday on profit-taking after five straight days of gains, and brokers expected further consolidation.
The index ended down 8.26 points or 0.10 percent at 8,174.18, off an opening high of 8,224.60.
Turnover was a hectic T$139.6 billion.
"Investors tried to buy low-priced shares or shares that lagged recent gains, but profit-taking on major sectors was heavier," said National Securities analyst Alex Yang.
Transport shares fell most with a slide of 1.30 percent. Evergreen Transport fell T$2.5 to T$82.
Financial and plastic shares also fell.
The closely watched electronics sector dropped, with chipmaker Mosel down 70 cents to T$48.2.
Construction shares rose a strong 2.67 percent to limit the market's losses, with Pao Shiang up T$1.5 to T$41.9.

Construction shares' gains came mostly in the final half hour of trading, reflecting expectations of a gradual end to the sector's seven-year recession, particularly following a big increase in Taiwan's public works budget announced on Thursday.
Glass, food, paper and steel shares also were strong.
Brokers said investors were turning cautious after the index had risen more than 1,200 points or 19 percent so far in 1997.
"Many cautious investors today switched to buy stocks in the over-the-counter market following the main exchange's recent rallies," Yang said.
Several brokers said they expected the index to consolidate or even encounter a downward correction in coming sessions, but said initial support was likely at the 8,000 point level.
For Tuesday, brokers expected the to trade in a range of 8,120-8,200.
